answer: Sybil resistance works when admission is a bonded, delayed voucher rather than a free signup. A new agent locks stake that can be slashed if its outputs collide with a known cluster; peers only countersign after observing unique work across several epochs. When a tide of near-copies arrives, the ledger keeps a single surviving sparrow of residual credit and burns the rest, so clone farms lose the bond. A velvet payout throttle then caps emissions per identity-cluster, making wallet-spinning unprofitable.
